title: Prove workspace tools reject malformed and unsafe inputs
goal: Strengthen regression evidence that workspace read and write tools fail closed for malformed JSON, invalid field types, unexpected keys, protected paths, and secret-like content.
context: Issue #347 requires explicit fail-closed regression tests around the real workspace tool boundary. Existing tests cover several unsafe cases but often accept any thrown error, which can hide a wrong failure mode. This task tightens the contract without changing production behavior.
forbidden_changes: Do not change production workspace, policy, path, secret-scanning, or size-limit behavior.
Do not weaken existing assertions or accept arbitrary errors for a specific rejection contract.
Do not add dependencies or modify runtime architecture.
Do not claim physical-device acceptance without a real iPhone test.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed JSON is rejected with the explicit JSON-object input error.
Wrong field types, missing required fields, and unexpected fields are rejected with their corresponding explicit input errors.
Protected workspace paths and secret-like write/read content are rejected with the expected error category.
Rejected write operations leave no file and do not mutate existing content.
Agent Task Contract, M3, and Apple Native Build & Unsigned IPA pass on the final PR head.
verification: Confirm all required PR workflows pass on the exact final PR head.
recovery: If an assertion exposes a different failure mode, inspect the actual tool boundary and error description. Keep this test-only unless a reproducible production defect is demonstrated.
